breathing.name: 2-Minute Breathing
breathing.short_description: A simple breathing exercise to slow down and settle in a few minutes
breathing.description: When anxiety strikes, your breathing becomes shallow and rapid. This technique teaches you simple breathing patterns that activate your body's natural relaxation response.

grounding.name: 5-4-3-2-1 Grounding
grounding.short_description: A sensory technique that pulls you out of anxious thoughts by focusing on what's around you right now
grounding.description: The grounding technique uses your five senses to bring you back to the present moment. Noticing 5 things you can see, 4 you can touch, 3 you can hear, 2 you can smell and 1 you can taste helps you step out of the cycle of anxious thoughts and reconnect with your surroundings.

guidedBreathing.name: Guided Breathing
guidedBreathing.short_description: Several guided rhythms, including coherent breathing, to slow down and ease tension
guidedBreathing.description: Follow guided breathing rhythms, with a visual cue to keep a slow, steady pace. Several rhythms are offered, depending on what you need: focusing, relaxing or taking a quick break.

progressiveMuscleRelaxation.name: Progressive Muscle Relaxation
progressiveMuscleRelaxation.short_description: Release physical tension by systematically tightening and relaxing muscle groups throughout your body
progressiveMuscleRelaxation.description: Anxiety often creates physical tension that you might not even notice. This technique teaches you to systematically tense and then release different muscle groups, helping you become aware of physical stress and learn to let it go. The contrast between tension and relaxation helps your body reach a deeper state of calm.

peacefulVisualization.name: Peaceful Visualization
peacefulVisualization.short_description: Guided, narrated mental imagery for a calm moment in a peaceful place
peacefulVisualization.description: Your imagination can create soothing moments. This technique guides you, with narration, through peaceful scenes that help you turn away from anxious thoughts and find a little tranquility. With practice, this calm becomes easier to return to.

thoughtLabeling.name: Thought Labeling
thoughtLabeling.short_description: A mindfulness technique that helps you recognize anxious thoughts as temporary mental events, not facts
thoughtLabeling.description: Anxious thoughts can feel overwhelming when you treat them as absolute truths. This mindfulness practice teaches you to observe your thoughts with curiosity rather than judgment. Learning to label thoughts as 'thinking,' 'worrying,' or 'planning' creates distance between yourself and your anxious mind, reducing their emotional impact.

stressReliefBubbles.name: Stress Relief Bubbles
stressReliefBubbles.short_description: Interactive bubble-popping activity that redirects anxious energy into playful, repetitive motion
stressReliefBubbles.description: Sometimes the best way to deal with anxiety is through gentle distraction and play. This simple interactive activity helps redirect nervous energy while giving your mind a break from anxious thoughts.

fidgetSpinner.name: Online Fidget Spinner
fidgetSpinner.short_description: Steady restless hands with a calm, repeatable spinning motion on any device.
fidgetSpinner.description: Spin, release, and watch the momentum unwind. The simple tactile focus gives your hands something consistent to do while your mind follows an unfussy visual pattern—useful when you need a quiet outlet for excess energy.

soundTherapy.name: Sound Therapy
soundTherapy.short_description: Soothing sounds and frequencies to support relaxation and focus
soundTherapy.description: Listening to soft, steady sounds can help you relax and quiet mental chatter. Choose the frequency and atmosphere that feel good to you. Use this therapy to create a calming environment that supports deep relaxation and stress relief.

stressBall.name: Stress Ball
stressBall.short_description: Interactive stress ball to squeeze away tension and redirect anxious energy through tactile engagement
stressBall.description: Sometimes physical tension needs a physical release. This virtual stress ball provides a satisfying tactile experience that helps channel nervous energy and anxiety into purposeful squeezing motions. The repetitive action helps calm your mind while giving your body a way to release built-up stress and tension.

worryTime.name: Worry Time
worryTime.short_description: Write down your worries and set them an appointment at a chosen time of day
worryTime.description: Rather than fighting worries, this technique suggests writing them down and coming back to them during a dedicated time of day. It helps you feel less at their mercy and take back some control.

leavesOnStream.name: Leaves on a Stream
leavesOnStream.short_description: Place your thoughts on leaves and watch them drift away, to gain distance
leavesOnStream.description: An Acceptance and Commitment Therapy exercise: you notice your thoughts, place them on leaves and let them drift with the current, without holding on or fighting them.

selfCompassion.name: Self-Compassion Break
selfCompassion.short_description: Three steps to speak to yourself kindly in a difficult moment
selfCompassion.description: A short three-step break, inspired by Kristin Neff, to acknowledge your difficulty, remember you're not alone and offer yourself some kindness.

thoughtRecord.name: Questioning a Thought
thoughtRecord.short_description: A guided CBT worksheet to examine an anxious thought and find a more balanced view
thoughtRecord.description: A step-by-step worksheet from cognitive behavioural therapy: describe the situation, spot the emotion and the thought, examine the facts, then find a fairer thought.
